data.title: Chat: mode.test.js AS-24 case is flaky under concurrent docker build — two independent observations

data.to:
Recurring-observation rule fired (CLAUDE.md: same issue in 2+ consecutive advances becomes a task). Two independent observations by two employees, one day apart, neither related to the diff under review at the time:

1. 2026-09-03, qa-priya during the AS-27 review (finding F5): "mode: AS-24 — API-mode writes land in the server view" failed at 1350ms on one of four full in-container runs, where it takes ~3000ms passing. Isolated re-run 9/9; two subsequent full runs 255/255. Recorded as a load flake, explicitly not filed, pending a second sighting.
2. 2026-09-04, developer-lena during AS-75 implementation: the same case (test/mode.test.js:93, the spawned-CLI assert.equal(dm.status, 0)) failed on one docker run and passed on the three runs before and after, and on every host run.

The second sighting is the trigger. Both observations share a signature: it fails only in-container, only under concurrent image build, and only on the spawned-CLI status assertion — never on the host, never in isolation.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A NORMAL FLAKE: this is the AS-24 guard, which exists to prove that host-side CLI writes cannot land in a DB view the server never sees. A guard that fails intermittently under load trains readers to re-run it, and a re-run habit on THIS guard is how the orphan-161 class of bug gets waved through. It also lands on the same runner every task now depends on for its cardinality claims — an intermittent red inflates the cost of every future mutation run.

LIKELY SHAPE (for the planner, not a conclusion): a spawned child process racing a timeout or a not-yet-ready server under CPU contention from a concurrent build. The failing assertion is on the child exit status, and the passing duration (~3000ms) against the failing one (1350ms) suggests the child exits early rather than hanging.

ACCEPTANCE: the flake is either reproduced deterministically under induced load and fixed at the root, or the test is made robust in a way that does NOT weaken what it asserts about the AS-24 mode boundary. A wider timeout that also lets a genuine mode regression pass is not acceptable — demonstrate by mutation that the hardened test still goes red when CLI writes are allowed to bypass the server.

provenance.reason: Board directive DM msg 557 (2026-09-07): Chat set before further core-product work
DM msg 557: Chat-first ordering (see AS-28 reason)

data.body: THIRD OBSERVATION (from the AS-95 review, agent:qa-priya, 2026-09-10). The mode.test.js AS-24 case failed on BOTH master and the AS-95 branch when the two compose suites were built concurrently, and passed on both when each was run solo. That clears the 2-consecutive-observations bar this task was filed against, and adds a detail the first two did not have: it is not branch-specific and not load-in-general -- it reproduces specifically under CONCURRENT docker build, which is what a reviewer does when establishing a master baseline alongside a branch run. Ruben saw the same shape in the AS-93 review (5 of 14 runs, both trees, clean when quiet) and correctly declined to file it as a single session; this is the confirmation. Operational cost, now measured twice: a reviewer must void and re-run a concurrent pair, which on AS-95 meant discarding a 292/293 and a 339/340 that were both false reds. Suggested framing for the eventual plan: PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS is 500ms at apps/chat/lib/client.js:21 and the probe is racing a loaded docker daemon, so the fix is either a longer//adaptive probe timeout or a test that does not depend on wall-clock probe latency -- and per M4 the plan must name the concrete concurrent-build input that makes the guard report the flake, satisfied by an observed red.

FOURTH OBSERVATION (AS-95 rework cycle 1, agent:developer-marcus, 2026-09-10). mode.test.js AS-24 failed once more on the first counted compose run of the AS-95 branch (362/363), green solo on the re-run. That is four independent observations across three tasks (AS-93 review, AS-95 review, AS-95 rework) and two different employees, on both master and branch trees. The operational cost is now consistent and measurable: every counted run of the chat suite has roughly a coin-flip chance of a false red under load, so reviewers and implementers must run twice and know which result to void -- and 'void the failing run' is a habit that will eventually void a TRUE red. That is the real risk here, not the wasted minutes.

Orchestrator (tick watcher:93997, loop tick 18): backlog -> in_planning, third lane beside the AS-73 review and AS-80 planning. Next by age in the Chat set behind AS-80. Planning is exploration and a written plan only: no docker invocation in this stage, because a concurrent build is this task's own flake condition and Ruben's counted compose run for AS-73 is in flight this tick. Planner: cto-owen as tech lead.

Plan written (cto-owen, tech lead, against master 5c98662; no docker in this stage). HYPOTHESES, ranked: H1 (primary) the child's only wall-clock-bounded step is the probe — client.js:48 AbortSignal.timeout(500) — and under emulated-amd64 CPU contention (31 test-file processes + a concurrent BuildKit build on one VM) the in-process server misses 500 ms; TimeoutError has no ECONNREFUSED code so probe() returns 'ambiguous' and rule 3 (chat.js:133-138) exits 1 with the AS-24 refusal, no DB touched. The arithmetic lands on the observed 1350 ms (~700 ms emulated node start + 500 ms budget + exit). H2 a parent-loop stall in the test process, same symptom, told apart by measuring probe latency (R0). H3 signal kill / start-up failure — weak, no 'null' status in four sightings. Ruled out on evidence: ECONNREFUSED (listen awaited before spawn), lazy first-request ingest (server.js:265 ingests before listen and stamps the throttle), DNS, any post-probe timeout (call() has none). DECIDED: (1) legibility first — run() returns elapsedMs+signal, describeExit() puts status/signal/elapsed/stderr/stdout in every status-0 assertion, and the refusal text itself names the reason ('timed out after N ms' vs HTTP/shape); (2) probe budget becomes an exported DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 3000 (time-boxed: moves only if R0 shows p99 > 1000 ms under load) plus a validated CHAT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS knob (usage error on bad values, empty = unset); (3) the two up-path cases pass 20000 via one apiEnv helper; the trap case keeps the default and asserts it; (4) the flake signature is pinned deterministically with a 150 ms delaying TCP proxy — budget 50 → exit 1 naming the timeout (T1), budget 20000 → up (T2) — same server, only the budget differs. Timeouts may move: the default and the knob. Must not move: timeout=>ambiguous, ambiguous=>exit 1 zero side effects, down requires ECONNREFUSED/ENOTFOUND, up requires 2xx+shape, no mid-command fallback or retry. WHY a wider budget cannot mask a mode regression: a budget only ever produces refusals; AC-5 proves it by mutation M1 (rule-3 'up' routed to the direct backend must red the AS-24 case, the sweep and T2 at the server-view assertion). Other mutations: M2 timeout->'down' reds {trap, T1}; M3 knob ignored reds {T1, T3}; M4 old budget under load reds >=1/3 then 3/3 green restored. Reproduction is implementation work, in order: R0 measure probe latency in-container (quiet / CPU-burn / concurrent build), R1 CPU-burn siblings in the test service, R2 the real condition (build beside the counted run) — observe red on unfixed code BEFORE fixing, 20-minute box; if it never reds, say so and T1 carries the mechanism. LEFT OUT deliberately: no probe retry loop, no timeout on call(), no --test-concurrency change (masking), healthcheck untouched, host-CLI-during-rebuild analog observed in the field not the suite. Host baseline 480/480 on master; predicted 484. Branch feat/AS-83-probe-budget. Implementer: developer-marcus (Lena acceptable). Reviewer: qa-ruben — Priya put the probe-timeout hypothesis on the record and must not certify her own framing; Marcus authors; Ruben's M6 mandate is to repeat R2 himself and probe the margin (150 ms delay vs 100/200 ms budgets).

Implementation (developer-marcus, tick watcher:93997, lane 3). Branch feat/AS-83-probe-budget: 6d31a64 (legibility+T4), f00f2c5 (probe reason + budget knob), 060c7dd (apiEnv/slowProxy/T1-T3 + amended trap case). Worktree clean, on branch.

FINDINGS FIRST (outside the criteria list):

F-1 AC-7 is unsatisfiable exactly as written, and I observed the red anyway. It asks the pre-fix load run to quote 'timed out after 500 ms' — but that reason string IS the fix (§3 step 2); at the legibility-only commit no reason exists to print. What the red actually shows, R1 on detached 6d31a64 (production code unfixed), 1 of 1 attempts red, BURNERS=20 on NPROC=10, 'Image as83test-test Built': 'post: exit 1 signal null after 2961 ms / --- stderr --- chat: something is listening at http://127.0.0.1:46557 but the probe failed; refusing to touch the shared DB directly ... (AS-24) ... CHAT_MODE=direct / --- stdout --- (empty)'. That is the rule-3 ambiguous refusal, so H1 is the mechanism and H3 is dead (signal null, not a kill). Two corrections to §1's arithmetic: elapsed was 2961 ms, not the predicted ~1350 ms (under 2x oversubscription node start-up dominates the 500 ms budget), and the sweep went red too (20.1 s), which the plan predicted only for the AS-24 case. Reviewer: the '500 ms' half of AC-7 cannot be evidenced at that commit by construction, only the refusal path can.

F-2 Deliberate deviation from the plan's M3 anchor. §8 anchors M3 on 'the single literal CHAT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS in resolveBackend'; that literal would have appeared twice there (the env read and its own error message), so the anchor was not unique. Implemented as a probeBudget() helper with one call site — 'const timeoutMs = probeBudget();' — and M3 replaces that line with DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS, which ignores the knob and skips validation in one edit. Same mutation, an anchor that can only hit the intended site.

F-3 Both grep-based criteria (AC-1, AC-3) are sensitive to prose, i.e. weak. My first draft of the describeExit doc comment contained the literal 'assert.equal(x.status, 0, x.stderr)' and made AC-1 read 19 vs 18; my first draft of the DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS comment contained '500 ms' and made AC-3 list two lines. Both passed only after I reworded English, not code. Counting comments is not counting assertions — treat these two as smoke, not proof; the mutations are the real guards.

F-4 The plan's §3 step 1 named 15 assertion lines; the file had 16 (now 18). AC-1 compares the two grep counts so it stays self-consistent, but the plan's enumerated line list was already stale against master.

F-5 Cost, accepted and visible: the trap case now spends the full 3000 ms default (host wall time 3.04 s for that case; whole host suite 7.8 s).

ACCEPTANCE SWEEP — a floor check, not the review. 9 of 12 evidenced, 3 not yet run.
AC-1 PASS: grep 'status, 0, ' = 18, grep 'status, 0, describeExit' = 18, zero bare .stderr messages; T4 green (covers the status-null/SIGKILL shape too).
AC-2 PASS: amended trap case asserts 'timed out after 3000 ms' via the imported constant and elapsedMs >= it; T1 asserts 'timed out after 50 ms'; one template in lib/client.js:89.
AC-3 PASS: DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS exported; grep '500|3000' lib/client.js lists exactly line 35.
AC-4 PASS: T1(50)/T2(20000)/T3(abc,0,-5 -> usage error with zero side effects; '' -> unset, exit 0) green; M3 killed reds exactly {T1, T3}.
AC-5 PASS: M1 killed reds exactly {AS-24 case, T2, sweep}, 10 pass / 3 fail, failing at mode.test.js:185, :288, :500 — every one a server-view assertion, none a timeout.
AC-6 PASS: M2 killed reds exactly {trap case, T1}, 11 pass / 2 fail; squatter and CHAT_MODE=api-with-down-server stayed green as predicted.
AC-7 PASS with the F-1 caveat: 1 of 1 R1 runs red on unfixed code, message quoted above.
AC-8 PARTIAL: R1 on the fixed branch 2 of 2 green (13/13 each, 'Image as83test-test Built' on both). R2 NOT RUN (tick time).
AC-9 NOT RUN: M4 needs R1 x3 either side of a rebuild; no budget left this tick.
AC-10 NOT RUN: R0 probe-latency p50/p99/max unmeasured. The default therefore stands at 3000 by the plan's own rule (it moves only if a measured p99 > 1000 ms), but it is unproven, not proven — say so in review.
AC-11 PASS: counted compose, -p as83test, 'run --build --rm test'. Merge-base e5de119 baseline 480 pass / 0 fail ('Image as83test-test Built'); branch 484 pass / 0 fail (same receipt). Delta exactly +4. Host 484 = compose 484, so host-minus-compose delta is 0 on both sides, same as master.
AC-12 PASS: git status --porcelain empty after every mutation and after the load runs; no stray apps/chat/data/chat.db; diff touches only lib/client.js, bin/chat.js, test/mode.test.js, README.md.

Mutation hygiene: each mutant hashed before, asserted applied at the site (occurrence counts plus the enclosing-function slice, and that the mutated call's *definition* still exists), run, restored in a finally, hash proven equal, tree proven clean; restored tree re-ran 484/484. Runner and raw logs in scratchpad/developer-marcus/AS-83/ (per-actor — reviewer should not read it).

REMAINING for the next implementation tick, in priority order: R2 (concurrent 'build --no-cache server' beside the counted suite, 3 runs), M4 (apiEnv budget -> '500' under R1, rebuild both halves), R0 (probe latency quiet/burn/build -> AC-10). Everything else is done and committed; the branch is green and self-consistent without them. Docker gate: Lena's AS-80 marker was already present, so no lane was disturbed; compose project as83test torn down with 'down --remove-orphans' (AS-106).

Orchestrator (cto-owen, tick watcher:93997 loop tick 19): stays in_progress for one more implementation tick rather than entering review. Marcus landed the full code change (6d31a64, f00f2c5, 060c7dd; host 484/0; compose -p as83test Built 484/484 vs merge-base 480/480; M1/M2/M3 killed with exact predicted sets; R1 observed red on unfixed code with the ambiguous refusal at 2961 ms, 2/2 green fixed) but the tick clock cut the remaining load work: R0 (probe latency p50/p99/max, which AC-10 requires and the 3000 ms default decision depends on), R2 (the concurrent-build condition, AC-8's other half) and M4 (AC-9). Sending it to review with three criteria unattempted would only buy a rework cycle. Next tick: Marcus resumes from scratchpad/developer-marcus/AS-83/progress.md, runs R0/R2/M4, records the numbers and the default decision in his comment, then the task moves to review (Ruben). His AC-7 'unsatisfiable as written' finding is for the reviewer to weigh; it is a plan-text defect, not a code one.

Implementation resumed and closed out the three load items left by the tick clock (tick watcher:93997, loop tick 20). Branch unchanged at 060c7dd — this tick was measurement and mutation, no code, nothing to commit. Drivers are scratch (r2-r0.mjs, m4.mjs in my own scratchpad), not committed.

FINDINGS FIRST (M5), then the criteria sweep as a floor check.

F-1 (restated from last tick, for the reviewer) — AC-7 is UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN. It asks for an observed red on UNFIXED code whose describeExit quotes both "refusing to touch the shared DB" AND "timed out after 500 ms". The second string does not exist in unfixed code: the reason text is introduced by §3 step 2, which IS the fix. At 6d31a64 (legibility only, production unfixed) the refusal cannot name its timeout. Observed red was: `post: exit 1 signal null after 2961 ms` + the full AS-24 ambiguous refusal, stdout empty, 1 of 1 runs red under BURNERS=20/NPROC=10. Satisfied in substance (H1 confirmed, H3 dead), not in letter. The criterion should have demanded the quote only from the fixed code; the reviewer should judge the substance, not the string.

F-2 — R0 AS SPECIFIED MEASURES A FLOOR, NOT THE SUITE CONDITION, and the numbers say so. The harness is a LONE node process in the container; at suite time the probing child competes with ~31 `node --test` processes and also pays spawn + module load, none of which R0 sees. Worst-of-50 under the heaviest available condition is 334.9 ms — BELOW the old 500 ms budget. So R0 on its own does NOT prove the 500 ms budget was the binding constraint; it corroborates direction and fixes the default. The mechanism rests on the AC-7 observed red and on T1 (deterministic). I am flagging this rather than letting the R0 table read as proof.

F-3 — p99 == max by construction at n=50 (the 99th-percentile index is the last sample). Read the p99 column as "worst of 50", not as a tail estimate.

F-4 — M4's red landed at the SWEEP case, not the dm/AS-24 case the plan predicted. Checked per the AS-95 sharpening before reporting: not a wrong-site mutation — the applied-at-site assertions pin the edit inside apiEnv ('20000' 0x, '500' 1x, and the '500' inside the apiEnv slice), and the failing assertion's own message quotes "(timed out after 500 ms)", i.e. the budget I changed. The sweep is mechanically the likelier loser: ~15 children through apiEnv, ~15x the exposure to one 500 ms budget that the dm case has. Same asymmetry as last tick's R1-unfixed, where the sweep also went red.

F-5 (deviation) — M4 ran 1 mutated + 1 restored run, not the plan's 3 + 3. Six loaded container runs at 53-97 s each did not fit before the 09:11Z hard kill. Recorded as a deviation, not a pass. Resume: `node m4.mjs` with M4_RUNS=3.

F-6 (for the merger) — AC-11's absolute 484 is measured against merge base e5de119. Master is now 12 commits ahead and its apps/chat moved (AS-73 roster-parity + org-chart/personnel tests): master host count is 486 today, so the post-merge expectation is 490, not 484. The surviving invariant is the delta +4; file sets are disjoint (mode.test.js vs roster-parity/org-chart/personnel), no interaction expected.

R2 (AC-8 other half) — counted compose suite on the fixed branch under a concurrent `docker compose -p as83test build --no-cache server` from the worktree. 3 of 3 GREEN: run 1 484/484/0 exit 0 41.85 s; run 2 484/484/0 exit 0 41.34 s; run 3 484/484/0 exit 0 39.49 s. Receipt on every run: `Image as83test-test Built`. LOAD ATTRIBUTION (AC-8 needs the condition attributable): the load was MY OWN background --no-cache server build, started 08:51:58Z and still alive at the end of all three runs (buildAliveAtEnd true on 1-3). NOT the sibling lanes — `docker ps` snapshotted before each run showed no as80test*/as74test* container at any point, only long-standing unrelated idle services (asc-chat-server-1, whatever-sticks-*, asc-invoicing-web-1, web, api, search, meilisearch, postgres). AS-80/AS-74 contributed nothing I can claim.

M4 (AC-9) — one indivisible step: sha before -> anchored replace of the single `CHAT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS: '20000'` in apiEnv with '500' -> four applied-at-site assertions -> rebuild + loaded run -> restore in finally -> sha equal + `git status --porcelain` empty -> rebuild + loaded run. Predicted: >=1 red then green. Observed: MUTATED 1 of 1 RED — 13 tests / 12 pass / 1 fail, exit 1, 53 s, rebuild receipt `Image as83test-test Built`; failing case `mode: AS-24 — full command sweep in API mode (no DB file, direct-mode shapes)` (14.83 s) with the message quoting "… refusing to touch the shared DB directly … (timed out after 500 ms)". RESTORED 1 of 1 GREEN — 13/13/0, exit 0, 97 s, rebuild receipt `Image as83test-test Built`. Restore proven: sha AFTER == sha BEFORE (2abd16dc…ac519), worktree porcelain empty. Both halves carry their own Built line, per the stale-image rule.

R0 (AC-10) — probe latency inside the test container, n=50 per condition, container nproc 10. quiet: p50 2.7 / p99 84.7 / max 84.7 ms. Concurrent --no-cache server build: p50 3.3 / p99 85.7 / max 85.7 ms. 20 cpu-burn siblings (2 x nproc): p50 5.3 / p99 334.9 / max 334.9 ms. DECISION ON THE DEFAULT: KEEP 3000 ms. The plan's §3 step-3 rule fires only if p99 under induced load exceeds 1000 ms; worst observed is 334.9 ms, so ceil(3 x p99 / 500) x 500 is NOT applied and DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS stays 3000. H1 vs H2: latency scales with load (2.7 -> 85 -> 335), it does not spike independent of it — the H1 signature. Read alongside F-2 and F-3.

ACCEPTANCE SWEEP — FLOOR CHECK ONLY (the list is a floor, not the review; 6 findings above sit outside it). AC-1 PASS: `status, 0, ` = 18 and `status, 0, describeExit` = 18; T4 passes. AC-2 PASS: trap case + T1 pass; one "timed out after" template in lib/client.js (line 89). AC-3 PASS: grep "500|3000" in lib/client.js lists exactly one line, `export const DEFAULT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 3000` (line 35); trap case asserts the 3000 ms text and elapsed >= 3000 via the imported constant. AC-4 PASS: T1/T2/T3 pass; M3 red set exactly {T1, T3} (11 pass / 2 fail, last tick). AC-5 PASS: M1 red set exactly {AS-24 case, sweep, T2} at mode.test.js:185/288/500 — all server-view assertions, none a timeout (10 pass / 3 fail, last tick). AC-6 PASS: M2 red set exactly {trap case, T1} (11 pass / 2 fail, last tick); squatter and "api with a down server" stayed green. AC-7 SATISFIED IN SUBSTANCE, NOT IN LETTER — see F-1. AC-8 PASS: R1 2 of 2 green (last tick) and R2 3 of 3 green (above), every run with a Built receipt, load attributed. AC-9 PASS AT REDUCED CARDINALITY — 1+1 instead of 3+3; see F-5. AC-10 PASS: numbers above, default decision stated with the rule. AC-11 PASS AS MEASURED AGAINST e5de119: host 484/0; counted compose 484 on the branch vs 480 at the merge base = delta +4; host-minus-compose delta 0 on both sides, same as master's. See F-6 for the post-merge number. AC-12 PASS: `git diff master...feat/AS-83-probe-budget --stat` touches only apps/chat/{lib/client.js,bin/chat.js,test/mode.test.js,README.md} (280 insertions, 46 deletions); no .lattice, no compose.yaml/Dockerfile, no package.json, no top-level markdown; `git -C .worktrees/AS-83 status --porcelain` empty after every mutation run.

NOT REACHED: nothing beyond F-5's reduced M4 cardinality. `docker compose -p as83test down --remove-orphans` was run at the end of last tick's docker work; this tick's runs were all `run --rm`, so no as83test container is left behind (the background build was killed by the driver). From my side the branch is ready for review; Ruben's M6 mandate (repeat R2 himself, and probe the 150 ms proxy against 100 ms and 200 ms budgets so the verdict flips AT the budget) is unaffected by anything here.

M4 upgraded to the plan's cardinality before the tick clock — F-5 (reduced 1+1) and part of F-4 are WITHDRAWN. Second indivisible execution (same recipe, same applied-at-site assertions, restore proven: sha equal to 2abd16dc…ac519, worktree porcelain empty, branch still 060c7dd) ran 2 mutated + 2 restored:

MUTATED (old 500 ms budget via apiEnv, under R1 load — 20 burners, container nproc 10): run A 13 tests / 10 pass / 3 fail exit 1, 41 s; run B 13 / 11 / 2 exit 1, 40 s. RESTORED: run A 13/13/0 exit 0, 86 s; run B 13/13/0 exit 0, 90 s. Every one of the four carries its own `Image as83test-test Built` line.

M4 TOTAL ACROSS BOTH EXECUTIONS: 3 of 3 mutated RED, 3 of 3 restored GREEN — the plan's 3+3, so AC-9 is a full pass and not a reduced-cardinality pass. Observed red set (union): {`mode: AS-24 — API-mode writes land in the server view; no DB file is ever created`, `mode: AS-24 — full command sweep in API mode`, `mode: AS-83 — the same slow server inside the budget is up` (T2)} — all three and only the three apiEnv consumers. Per run: {sweep} / {dm, sweep, T2} / {dm, sweep}.

This corrects F-4: the dm/AS-24 case the plan predicted DID go red, in both of the new runs. Run 1's sweep-only red was the weakest draw of a nondeterministic mutant, not a wrong-site edit — exposure ordering (sweep ~15 children > dm 1 child) shows up as which cases fall first, with the sweep red in 3 of 3. T2 going red is the sharpest single data point in the whole task: a genuinely live server behind a 150 ms proxy, refused as ambiguous once the budget is 500 ms and the box is loaded, and accepted at 20000 ms on the same run — the flake, with only the budget changed.

Unchanged from the previous comment: R2 3 of 3 green with attribution, R0 numbers and the decision to keep 3000 ms, findings F-1/F-2/F-3/F-6, and the AC floor sweep (with AC-9 now a clean pass). Nothing else not reached.
